verdicts.title: chunked_nll still missing from the alignment trainers guide
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced directly. docs/alignment/trainers.md:109-110 reads '`loss_type` selects the per-example head: "nll" (standard cross-entropy) or "dft" (Dynamic Fine-Tuning)' and line 62 shows 'loss_type="nll", # or "dft"'; `grep -rn chunked docs/alignment/` returns zero hits. chunked_nll is a real, supported value: guarded at packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trl/_sft_trainer.py:185 (rejects compute_loss_func), dispatched at :231-235 (forces fused_linear_cross_entropy, self._loss_fn=None), and covered by tests test_compat_trl_sft.py:78 and test_trl_trainers.py:233/398/447. docs/reference/transformers.md:472 documents all three values, so the two docs disagree. Pure documentation omission; nothing in the code or accounting changes. No open issue in issues-open.tsv covers this doc site (#323 is about trainer behavior vs contracts, not this table).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user reading the alignment trainers guide sees an apparently exhaustive two-value loss_type menu and never learns the logits-free fused chunked_nll path exists, or is confused when docs/reference/transformers.md:472 lists a third value the guide omits. One-line doc fix; no runtime or privacy consequence.

verdicts.title: mf_band + sampling_mode='poisson' pairs a plain Poisson sampler with cyclic-Poisson horizon accounting, underreporting epsilon
verdicts.reasoning: Every link verified. (1) Config: _training_arguments.py:188 `"mf_band": frozenset({"b_min_sep", "poisson"})`, validation at :1048 only checks membership, and test_config.py:549 `test_mf_band_accepts_poisson_override` pins it; docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:142 advertises `b_min_sep (or explicit poisson)`. (2) Accounting: _dpftrl.py:138-154 builds `_ftrl_poisson(mf_gaussian(nm, BandMfStrategy), ...)` -> CyclicPoisson; its pld_at (dpftrl/amplification/_poisson.py:178-214) computes `num_groups = ceil(rounded/bands)` and returns `poisson_gaussian_pld(nm/sensitivity, q).self_compose(num_groups)`. BandMfStrategy.sensitivity (_band_mf.py:128-130) ignores min_sep/max_participations and returns the coefficient column norm; I measured it to be exactly 1.0 at n_steps=1600, bands=16, so effective_nm == nm and the accountant is literally the ceil(n/bands)-fold Poisson-Gaussian composition (measured eps(1e-6)=0.9542 at nm=1, q=0.01, n=1600, bands=16 — identical to repeat(poisson(gaussian(1.0),0.01),100)). (3) Runtime: _dpftrl.py:224-233 returns `PoissonSampler` from opaque.dpsgd.sampling (independent Bernoulli(q) over the whole dataset every step). The matching `CyclicPoissonSampler` is only built for sampling_mode='cyclic_poisson', which no mechanism allows. (4) Both feed the run: _dp_trainer.py:1467 builds the amplifier from the same `a.sampling_mode` used at :3704 to build the sampler, and :4227 wraps it for calibration and epsilon reporting. The ceil(n/bands)-composition reduction is the amplified-BandMF result (Choquette-Choo et al. 2023) and holds only under one participation per bands-wide window. Under plain Poisson the per-band-window inclusion probability is 1-(1-q)^bands, not q, so the accounted mechanism is strictly weaker than the deployed one; already at bands=2, n=2 the deployed mixture puts mass 1-(1-q)^2 on a nonzero shift while the accountant charges only q, so it is provably not an upper bound. Not covered by an open issue: #699/#697 are prefix-tightening (and closed upstream), #356/#320 ('a mismatch between runtime and accounting raises before training') are closed as completed, and open #359 is about BandMfStrategy.sensitivity being participation-blind — this finding is the concrete, shipped, tested end-to-end pairing plus a composition-count mismatch (n/bands vs n) that #359 does not mention, so it is a materially worse instance rather than a duplicate.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user sets privacy_noise_mechanism='mf_band' with the documented sampling_mode='poisson' override (bands=16 default). The accountant charges ceil(n_steps/bands) compositions of a Poisson-Gaussian at per-participation sensitivity 1 — the cyclic-group reduction — while the deployed sampler draws every example independently at every step with no band separation. At nm=1, q=0.01, n=1600, bands=16 the reported/calibrated eps(1e-6) is 0.954; the identity-sampling reference over the same 1600 steps is 2.65, and a per-band-window-rate reference (100 groups at rate 1-(1-q)^16=0.148) is 12.0, so the reported epsilon understates the deployed mechanism by at least ~2.8x and likely far more, growing with bands. No warning is emitted; training completes and the accountant record stores the invalid bound.

verdicts.title: BallsInBins.pld_at docstring claims K-epoch reparameterization for BSR/BiSR/lambda-CGD and carries an unreachable BLT pinned-prefix gram branch
verdicts.reasoning: Verified by reading _balls_in_bins.py:133-244. The guard at :181-191 returns self.pld_at(self.n_steps, ...) for every non-Identity strategy whenever `rounded < self.n_steps`, so the BLT branch (:216-235) and the BSR/BiSR/lambda-CGD branch (:236-244) can only run with rounded == self.n_steps. Since `rounded` and `num_epochs_K` are derived solely from `rounded`, the full-horizon call computes the identical quantities, so `coefs[:rounded]` is always the whole pinned column and `gram_matrix(n_steps=rounded)` is always the full-horizon gram: the prefix differentiation in those two branches is dead. The docstring at :150-156 describes K_epochs reparameterization and an N-pinned K-prefix BLT gram, then states at :156-158 that correlated-strategy Monte Carlo paths use the full-horizon bound for every nonzero prefix — internally inconsistent, though the last sentence does state the actual behavior, which limits the harm. Behavior is conservative: the K-prefix release is a coordinate projection (post-processing) of the causal N-step release, so the full-horizon PLD dominates any prefix. No epsilon impact. Open prefix-tightening issues (#694/#696/#698/#700; #699/#697 already closed upstream) track making these prefixes tighter, not the docstring contradiction or the dead branch, so not a duplicate.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: No user-visible defect: every reachable non-Identity call already returns the full-horizon PLD, which is a valid conservative bound. The cost is maintenance: a contributor implementing the prefix-tightening issues reads the first half of the pld_at docstring, believes the K-epoch gram and BLT pinned-prefix paths are live and exercised, and removes the :181 guard — enabling code (notably the coefs[:rounded] slice, whose validity as a K-prefix bound was never established) that no existing test can reach with rounded < n_steps.

verdicts.title: accounting.md documents a 'hypergeometric prefix mixture' for k_out_of_t that the Python surface never computes
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced. docs/user-guide/accounting.md:180-183 says 'pld_at(K) accounts the hypergeometric prefix mixture; the full k>1 PLD uses the conservative Feldman-Shenfeld block reduction', implying k>1 prefixes grow through a hypergeometric mixture. In the shipped code KOutOfT.pld_at (_k_out_of_t.py:93-107) short-circuits every `n_steps < self.n_steps and total_participations > 1` query to pld_at(self.n_steps); the Rust entry (random_allocation.rs:291-299) delegates k==1 to the exact random-allocation prefix before any hypergeometric weight is formed, and its own doc comment (:266-270) says the Python wrapper snaps k>1 prefixes to the full-horizon block bound. The hypergeometric-cap branch (:301-318) is therefore unreachable from Python. Measured on this tree: KOutOfT(gaussian(1.0), k=2, n=8).pld_at(K).epsilon_at(1e-6) = 4.766211 for K in {1,3,7,8} (identical), while k=1 grows 2.430 -> 2.662 -> 2.835 -> 2.861. The returned value is a valid upper bound, so no epsilon risk — only an over-promise in the user guide. Open #441 (prefix may be conservative beyond the hypergeometric/block-cap strategy) and #693 (derive a k>1 prefix PLD) track making the bound tighter, not the user guide asserting the tighter behavior already ships, so not a duplicate.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user planning a k-out-of-t run with k>1 reads the guide, expects mid-run epsilon to grow with released steps through a hypergeometric prefix mixture, and budgets for an early stop; instead epsilon_at returns the full-horizon value from step 1 onward (verified: identical 4.76621 at K=1,3,7,8 for k=2, n=8), so a budget monitor trips immediately or the early-stop plan is unusable. The reported number is still a valid upper bound; only the documentation is wrong.

verdicts.title: b-min-sep warm-start likelihood ratio misnormalizes the stationary mixture
verdicts.reasoning: The mathematical defect is confirmed independently and decisively. mc.rs:69-75 computes `sum_f = f[0] + p*sum_{j=1}^{b-1} f[j]/denom` with denom = 1+(b-1)p, dividing only the barred-start terms. The module's own sampler sample_x_under_p (mc.rs:85-108) starts in the stationary state (state 0 w.p. 1/denom, state j w.p. p/denom), whose exact density ratio is (f[0] + p*sum f[j])/denom. I wrote an independent exact enumeration of P(y)/Q(y) over all warm-start participation patterns (scratchpad/vfy_lr.py) and compared it to both formulas at bands=2,3 and n=8..10: the corrected formula matches exact enumeration to ~1e-15 in every case, while the shipped formula overstates it by factors 1.048-1.171 (b=2,p=0.05 -> 1.0475; b=2,p=0.2 -> 1.164; b=3,p=0.1 -> 1.167). So the shipped statistic is not the likelihood ratio of any initial-state mixture (E_Q of it is 1+(b-1)p/denom > 1, measured 1.046 and 1.227). Consequence: since r_code > r_true pointwise, ln(r) samples inflate the remove-direction PLD (conservative) and -ln(r) samples deflate the add-direction PLD (anti-conservative). Independent MC quantification (scratchpad/vfy_lr_eps.py, 200k/100k samples, delta=1e-2): repo smoke config (coef=[sqrt.7,sqrt.3], n=50, p=0.05) CODE remove 1.271 / add 0.719 vs TRUE remove 1.224 / add 0.766; wider config (16 equal bands, p=0.02, denom=1.30) CODE remove 1.390 / add 0.381 vs TRUE remove 1.178 / add 0.585. I checked the consumer: PrivacyLossDistribution::epsilon_at returns the max over adjacencies (pld/mod.rs:266-293) and no Python API exposes the add side alone, so in every configuration I could construct the (inflated) remove side binds and the user-visible epsilon is over-stated by 4-18% — an error in the conservative direction, i.e. silent over-noising after calibration, not a privacy loss. The anti-conservative add-side component is real but latent: making it bind would require composing with a mechanism whose add-direction asymmetry exceeds the ~0.6 remove-add gap, which I could not exhibit. That is why I downgrade high -> medium. Reachable from opaque.dpftrl.accounting.b_min_sep, the default sampler for mf_band. No test compares bands>=2 output to any oracle (mc.rs tests are smoke/self-consistency). Not tracked: #697 (prefix tightness + MC error certification) is closed and is about uncertainty, not a wrong functional; open #359 is about BandMF sensitivity, open #666 is about regression vectors.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Any BandMF + b-min-sep run (the default sampler for privacy_noise_mechanism='mf_band') is priced with a statistic that is not the warm-start likelihood ratio: verified against exact enumeration, the shipped value exceeds the true P(y)/Q(y) by a factor up to denom = 1+(bands-1)p. Because epsilon_at takes the max over adjacencies and the inflated remove side always bound in my tests, the practical effect is an over-stated epsilon — 1.271 vs 1.224 at the repo's own smoke config and 1.390 vs 1.178 at 16 bands with p=0.02 (delta=1e-2) — i.e. calibration selects a larger-than-necessary noise multiplier and utility is silently lost. The mirror-image deflation of the add-direction PLD (0.381 vs a true 0.585 in the 16-band config) makes that component an invalid bound; it is currently masked by the max but would understate epsilon in any composition where the add adjacency binds.

verdicts.title: b-min-sep Monte Carlo epsilon depends on Rayon thread count with a fixed seed
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end on this tree. mc.rs:360-378 partitions the MC work by `rayon::current_num_threads().max(1)` and seeds each shard `seed+tid` (remove) / `seed+1000+tid` (add), so the drawn sample set depends on the machine's core count; bandmf_b_min_sep_prepare_transcripts (mc.rs:174-218) deliberately mirrors the same thread partition, and the Python transcript cache key (_transcript_cache.py) does not include the thread count. Measured through the public native entry with a fixed seed=173, coef=[sqrt(0.7),sqrt(0.3)], n=50, p=0.05, sigma=1.0, mc_resolution=5e-3, mc_failure_probability=1e-2: epsilon_at(1e-2) = 1.5788540210820663 (RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1), 1.5938243242558099 (2), 1.8443435849560390 (8) — a 17% swing from core count alone. The sibling balls-in-bins path solves exactly this with fixed 1024-sample shards and shard_seed(seed, shard, add_direction) (balls_in_bins/monte_carlo.rs:43-55), plus a Rust test and packages/opaque-accounting/tests/test_balls_in_bins_reproducible.py; random allocation has an equivalent test. There is no analogous mechanism or test for b_min_sep, which is the default sampler for mf_band. The seed+1000+tid collision only bites above 1000 Rayon workers — a real but negligible edge. Each individual value remains a valid confidence bound for its own sample set, so this is nondeterminism of the reported guarantee rather than an invalid one. Not a duplicate: open #666 asks for MC regression vectors (a test gap this defect would block), #697 (closed) covered prefix tightness and MC-error certification, and the closed #331 fix covered only balls-in-bins.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A team pins a seed for a BandMF + b-min-sep run and gets a different reported epsilon on different hardware: with everything else identical, epsilon_at(1e-2) is 1.579 on 1 Rayon worker, 1.594 on 2, and 1.844 on 8 (measured). Calibration on a many-core box therefore selects a different noise multiplier than the same configuration on a CI runner, and a published (epsilon, delta, seed) triple cannot be reproduced by a third party. Each value is still a valid confidence bound for the samples it drew, so the failure is silent nondeterminism of the guarantee, not an invalid bound.
